summary: Hold: the o m=128 half is already disproved by kernel times, since the NN 128x64 plan ran 5.5 us in 37ed8722 against the TN plan's 5.4 us on today's board and the board's o row is already 7.23 us, the same as the claimed 7.24 target. The qkv m=128 NN half is untried, but its best plausible gain is about 0.35% of headline. The hypothesis itself sizes the whole thing at +0.07-0.34%, far under the 1.24% bar, and its stacking partner (pooler-khalf-m128-fp32-partials-triton-castadd) is on hold.
justification: A. (i) o m=128: the evidence cited, 'judged 7.68 -> 7.24 us in 37ed8722', is run-to-run drift and not a layout effect. In that run SGLang's own o verify_16 row also moved from 7.68 to 7.36 us. At kernel level, the NN plan (nvjet_sm90_tst_128x64_64x8_1x2_h_bz_NNT) took 5.5 us. Master's current TN plan (..._TNT) takes 5.4 us on the 1.2794 board (3e3ffc5a), where the o row is 7.23 us at 1.013x SGLang. The NN copy picks the same 128x64 tile with the operand transposed, so nothing is left to win. The gap that remains (7.23 row vs 5.4 kernel vs 4.0 floor) is about 1.8 us of row-minus-kernel overhead, which no plan swap touches. (ii) qkv m=128: master already runs this cell on a cuBLASLt TN plan (nvjet 40x64 4x2 TNN, 15.7 us kernel, 16.07 us row, floor 8.4), and since 62da2d9e that plan is ranked and gated under a read flush. NN plans on a [8192, 2304] copy have not been tried here. The pooler NN analogy (-10% at m=128) is weak: the pooler went through torch.mm, where a layout change switches cuBLAS's heuristic family, whereas this cell already searches Lt heuristic plans directly. Even a 10% kernel cut is about 1.6 us on verify_16 (70.8 us summed row time). At about 0.235%/us that is about 0.37% of headline, and a 3% gate win is about 0.1%. Staleness: the change is written against blob 2bcfe7d4. Master is now a36f3392, which already has the flush_mode='read' keyword (CELL_FLUSH_MODES), the read-flush ranking and gate in _lt_prepare, the bulk12 cells and the khalf/router-PDL landings. So the change paragraph's 'new keyword flush_mode=read' already exists, and its 'keep cell B's TN choice exactly as today' now means the read-flush plan, not the plan the hypothesis assumed. The `prior` field is honest about bf16-verify-per-cell-cublaslt-plan-selector (in Do-not-try, neutral), but sub-change (i) repeats that prior's o NN mechanism unchanged, and the prior's own kernel data refutes it. Weakest link: the o 'gain' is entirely drift. With it removed, the hypothesis is a single sub-1% qkv probe that needs a C++ Lt module rebuild and 54 MB of extra weight copies per state.
confounders: phasec-pc-lt-qkv128-readflush (landed on master 62da2d9e, not in churn's landed list): it already re-ranked and re-gated the qkv m=128 TN Lt plan under the read flush, so the 'today's TN plan' this A/B compares against is the newly picked one. Any qkv NN win or loss is measured against a plan picked by the same machinery and inside the same row noise.

combo-rowowner-reduce-free-m1-qkv-o-plus-naive (landed): it introduced cell B (_LT_CPP / MuseLtDesc, TN only). This change rebuilds that module under a new LT_EXT_NAME, so a build or plan regression in cell B would mix with the NN effect.
Run-level drift on verify_16: SGLang's o m=128 baseline varies by 4% between runs (7.33-7.68 us), larger than the ~0.1-0.4 us effects predicted for either cell.
interference: No companion would rescue this. The effects predicted per cell (o ~0 us given kernel parity; qkv 0-1.6 us) sit inside the per-row and per-run noise. An ab-revert or control run would double the cost of a hypothesis whose best plausible headline is about 0.4%. If the qkv NN idea is ever worth checking, it should be a prepare-time-only measurement: rank NN against TN Lt plans under the read flush and log the result, with no routing change. If it shows a 10% or larger kernel cut, it can be folded into a larger verify_16 stack. It does not justify a judge check alone.
open_questions: Does cuBLASLt's heuristic return any qkv m=128 NN plan with a different tile family (not 40x64 4x2) on the H200? If NN only yields the same tiles transposed, sub-change (ii) has no mechanism either.

Is the ~1.8 us row-minus-kernel overhead on o m=128 (7.23 row vs 5.4 kernel) addressable at all, for example by a PDL chain or launch hiding? That gap, not the GEMM plan, separates o from its 4.0 us floor.
